after.text:
Since Heath-Brown’s work, the area of moments has seen great developments. In the early
2000s, Keating and Snaith [KS00b] made remarkable conjectures about all the moments of
ζ(s) by drawing analogies between the zeta-function and characteristic polynomials of large
random matrices. Progress towards these general conjectures has been achieved on multiple
fronts, from proving upper bounds conditional on RH for all the moments of ζ(s), to obtaining
unconditional lower bounds for all the moments and unconditional upper bounds for small k.
We will describe the Keating-Snaith conjectures in Section 2, and the subsequent progress
towards them in Section 3.

section_entries.label: 3.2-3.3. Unconditional upper and lower bounds and applications
section_entries.mathematical_role: States upper- and lower-bound propagation principles from twisted moments and notes an alternative large-deviation route and broader applications.

unit_result_entry.title: Twisted anchor moments propagate unconditional upper bounds downward
unit_result_entry.why_material: Formulates the principle that computing a moment with room to spare—equivalently with a short Dirichlet-polynomial twist—can yield sharp upper bounds for smaller moments. The zeta implementation combines an iterative scheme with a twisted fourth-moment input to reach the full interval from zero to two.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The earlier discrete fractional ranges are included to show what the propagation principle improves.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the operative principle is prose-complete; exact k-ranges and the fourth-moment anchor are notation-dependent.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Harper's multiscale Taylor and exceptional-set iteration
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Refines the two-range method into many prime blocks, assigns decreasing powers as prime size grows, approximates exponentials by truncated Taylor polynomials on good sets, and shows bad blocks occur on sets too small to matter. Flexible truncation and length choices keep each resulting Dirichlet polynomial inside available mean-value theorems.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Twisted mean values propagate lower bounds on both sides of the first moment
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Summarizes how short Dirichlet-polynomial twists turn a computable mean value into sharp lower bounds above an anchor and how a twisted second moment also reaches below the first moment. It contrasts this interpolation-like route with an independent route through lower bounds for large deviations in Selberg's central limit theorem.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: A moment computable with a short Dirichlet-polynomial insertion acts as an anchor: upper bounds propagate to smaller moments, while suitable first- and second-moment anchors propagate lower bounds above and below the first moment.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The survey states these principles only roughly; exact admissible twists, errors, and family hypotheses must be recovered from the cited works before theorem-level use.
